propositions: Type-tier comparability (epic tier 2, story tier 1, task/bug tier 0) incorrectly rejects valid dependencies between sibling tickets under the same parent, escalating to the common parent instead and creating invalid self-blocking edges.
Redundancy detection occurs before link resolution, so pairs that are well-formed inputs become redundant only after promotion but escape rejection, allowing ancestor-blocking edges to be written.

Blocking link resolution should use structural comparability (nearest common ancestor of both endpoints in the full ancestor chain) rather than type tier, enabling any two direct children of the same parent to link unchanged and cross-subtree dependencies to escalate to NCA children.

Post-resolution redundancy detection must reject any blocking pair whose resolved endpoints are in an ancestor-descendant relationship, catching both direct parent-child cases and escalated grandparent-grandchild pairs.

Non-blocking relations (relates_to, duplicates, supersedes, discovered_from, caused_by) must continue to record the original pair with original-pair redundancy logic, unchanged by blocking-relation restructuring.
The ancestor walk must terminate on cycles and walk to the true root instead of capping at two hops, enabling correct NCA resolution for chains deeper than epic-story-task.
